6805 bearing support

Independent assembly · 4 mm wall · Existing 40 mm travel screw + bearing ring

100%

Back the four shared motor bolts out 6 mm, keeping them captured in the holder. Slide the module off the shaft and lift it clear, then fully withdraw the bolts. Support the now-unfastened motor during service. The screw and bearing leave the holder from its motor-facing recess. Loosen the coupling first.

The bearing carries axial load into the wall. The existing D-shaft clamp remains accessible through the open holder.

6805
4mm
30.3mm
Rear

Four shared NEMA17 bolts and reinforced side walls

Four M3×40 screws pass through the holder and wall directly into the motor’s existing 31 × 31 mm holes. There are no separate holder bolts or locknuts. Continuous left and right shells connect the mounting corners to the bearing seat, while top and bottom openings leave the coupling clamp accessible. The motor-facing recess and uninterrupted outer-race lip retain the 6805 in the load direction.

Existing screw + bearing ring

The original helix, D bore and bolt/nut pockets are retained. The added ring has a Ø24.9 mm journal and Ø27 mm shoulder, occupying X22.3–31.3 mm. The coupling split stays open through the added material.

1 mm shorter holder

The holder projects 30.3 mm from the front of the 4 mm wall, reduced from 31.3 mm. The motor and screw keep their existing relative positions. The wall is 52 × 52 × 4 mm with only the four NEMA17 mounting holes. The T8 Z holder uses the same design with 2 mm recessed bolt heads to suit its thicker base wall.

Motor-facing recess

The bearing recess is Ø37.2 mm. Its forward lip contacts only the outer race, with 0.1 mm nominal axial clearance. The rear bearing-loading path stays clear. The 360° lip is uninterrupted by screw-access slots. Four M3×40 screws clamp the holder and wall to the motor, with 5.7 mm nominal motor-thread engagement. Thrust toward the screw tip passes into the wall; reverse-direction retention relies on the coupling.

Geometry checks

Loading validation…

All 41 sampled exploded-assembly poses are free of solid intersections. Access envelopes verify the captured-bolt removal sequence and hex-key approach. Separate checks verify the mounting columns, continuous lip, screw-head seats and nominal motor-thread engagement. The bearing leaves from the motor side; it never passes through the holder’s front lip. Sampling checks rigid clearances, not installation forces.

Designed around the earlier 1 lb (4.45 N) static input. The load path is positively retained toward the screw tip; this is still a prototype without a physically tested load rating. CAD checks do not establish PETG creep life, fatigue or vibration resistance. Bearing internals are reference envelopes. This bearing does not prevent back-driving when the motor is unpowered.

Geometry report · Assembly pose report

Assembly and hardware

  1. Seat the 6805 in the recess on the motor-facing side of the holder.
  2. Feed the screw’s threaded end through the bearing and holder from the motor side, until its shoulder reaches the bearing’s inner race. Fit the original clamp nut and bolt loosely.
  3. Hold the motor against the wall and slide the support module onto the shaft. Fit four M3×40 screws from the holder front through the wall into the motor. Start all four before tightening evenly. Verify the motor accepts 5.7 mm screw engagement without bottoming out.
  4. Gently seat the screw toward its tip until the outer race rests against the housing lip, then tighten the coupling in that seated position without preloading the motor shaft. Check free rotation before loading.

Print the wall flat; print the holder with its front face on the bed and columns upward. An actual P2S / Generic PETG / 0.20 mm slice with automatic supports enabled generates zero support extrusion for the holder (slice report). The T8 holder’s shallow head recesses produce 0.07 g of support confined to four pockets open to the bed; its bearing tunnel stays support-free (T8 holder slice report). Check actual PETG fits before loading. Full build notes and hardware list.
